questions.question: What is a function in programming?
options: A file containing an entire application
A named, reusable block of code that takes inputs and typically returns an output
questions.explanation: A function packages a set of instructions under a name so it can be called repeatedly with different inputs (arguments), instead of rewriting the same logic each time.

questions.question: When engineers say a project "imports" a library such as PyTorch or an LLM provider SDK, what is happening?
options: The script is creating a new file called torch
The script is pulling in an existing library/module's already-written functionality to reuse it
The script is deleting the torch library
The script is renaming the OpenAI SDK
questions.explanation: An import statement brings in functionality from an existing module, package, or library so the current script can reuse it without rewriting it from scratch.

questions.question: Engineering debates whether to write custom retry logic or import an existing library like `tenacity`. Which question best helps a TPM evaluate this trade-off?
options: Which option requires fewer lines of code today, regardless of anything else?
Is retry logic a well-solved, generic problem that an established library already handles well, and if we depend on it, who maintains that library?
Can we avoid making this decision entirely?
Does the library have a colorful logo?
questions.explanation: The core trade-off is whether the problem is generic and well-solved (favoring a maintained library) versus specific to the product (favoring custom code), plus the ongoing risk of depending on an external maintainer.
